solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: One uses trickery to climb eastern slope

blocks.note: to mount a hill is to climb it
E is the standard abbreviation for east or eastern
a bank is a sloping stretch of ground

explanation.surface: A climber heads up an eastern slope, though the opening words hint at a cheat.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition sits at the front and reads like part of the climbing story, which hides it well.
explanation.definitionFit: A mountebank is a charlatan or swindler, historically a quack selling fake remedies from a platform, so a person who deceives.

clue.text: Scientific instrument trashed in comic prose

indicators.note: something trashed is wrecked and thrown about, so the letters are scrambled into a new order

blocks.note: the ten letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A critic pans a lab instrument as rubbished in some funny writing.
explanation.definitionFit: A microscope is a laboratory device with lenses for magnifying very small objects, a classic piece of scientific apparatus.

clue.text: Run off for large teapot

indicators.note: off here means gone wrong or out of order, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the three letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone dashes off to fetch a big pot of tea.
explanation.definitionFit: An urn is a big metal vessel with a tap, used for making tea or coffee in quantity at gatherings.

clue.text: After time, currency is in difficulty

indicators.note: after tells us the second piece is placed following the first one

blocks.note: T is the standard abbreviation for time
the rouble is the currency of Russia

explanation.surface: Given enough time, a money system ends up struggling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is in' looks like the start of the phrase 'in difficulty', but only 'difficulty' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Trouble and difficulty are synonyms as nouns, both meaning problems or a state of distress.

clue.text: Black cat’s spring

blocks.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
the ounce is another name for the snow leopard, a big cat

explanation.surface: A dark-coated cat leaps into action.
explanation.walkthrough: The ounce is a crossword favourite for the snow leopard; the apostrophe-s reads as 'is', joining wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A bounce is a leap or rebound, so a spring in the sense of a jump.

clue.text: Secures what are on hand

blocks.note: first meaning: fastens something down with metal pins
second meaning: the hard tips growing on the fingers

explanation.walkthrough: 'on hand' looks like the idiom for available, but it is literal: things physically on the hand.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means fastens with hammered spikes, while the plural noun names the horny plates at the ends of fingers.

clue.text: Huge stone finally going in the mail, remarkably

indicators.note: finally points to the very end of the word that follows, so only its closing letter is kept
remarkably suggests something done in an unusual way, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the last letter of going
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A massive rock is somehow arriving by post.
explanation.definitionFit: A megalith is a large prehistoric standing block, like those at Stonehenge, literally a great rock.

clue.text: Is not able to love section of long poem

blocks.note: can't means is not able, written without its apostrophe
love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone is incapable of loving.
explanation.definitionFit: A canto is one of the major divisions of an epic poem, such as Dante's Inferno or Byron's Don Juan.

clue.text: One, or many teams so called

blocks.note: first meaning: joined together as a single whole
second meaning: the word that ends the names of many football clubs

explanation.walkthrough: Many British football clubs carry this word in their names, such as Manchester United, Leeds United and Newcastle United.
explanation.definitionFit: Joined into a single body means made into one, and the word is a common suffix in football club names.

clue.text: An old man myself, so fit to turn up

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means reading the letters from bottom to top, so backwards

blocks.note: the setter refers to themself as me
so and thus both mean therefore
hale means healthy, as in hale and hearty

explanation.surface: An elderly man claims he is fit enough to show up.
explanation.walkthrough: Methuselah is the Bible's longest-lived man, said to have reached 969 years.
explanation.definitionFit: Methuselah is the biblical patriarch famed for great age, so his name is used for any very aged person.

clue.text: I’m surprised, first to meet a measure of resistance

indicators.note: first to points at the opening of the word that follows, so only its initial letter is kept

blocks.note: oh is an exclamation of surprise
the first letter of meet

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims in surprise at being first to encounter some opposition.
explanation.definitionFit: The ohm is the SI unit of electrical resistance, so it quantifies how strongly a conductor opposes current.

clue.text: Assembled, as keen as this, may we hear?

indicators.note: asking what we may hear means the word is identified by its sound when spoken

blocks.note: keen as mustard is a British idiom for very eager

explanation.surface: A sergeant asks whether the gathered troops are eager.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'keen as mustard' means extremely enthusiastic, so 'this' stands for the condiment.
explanation.definitionFit: To muster troops is to gather them together for inspection, so mustered means gathered into one group.

clue.text: Supports fast bowling as key

blocks.note: to back someone is to support them
in cricket, pace bowling is fast bowling

explanation.surface: A cricket fan backs the fast bowlers as crucial to the team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'key' reads as an adjective meaning crucial, but it is a keyboard key; in cricket, pace bowlers deliver the ball fast.
explanation.definitionFit: Backspace is a computer keyboard button that deletes the character before the cursor.

clue.text: Having money, we brought back nut-tree

indicators.note: brought back suggests returning the way it came, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: cash is money
taken as written, before turning round

explanation.surface: Once we had funds, we imported a tree that bears nuts.
explanation.definitionFit: The cashew is a tropical evergreen whose kidney-shaped seed is eaten, so it names both the plant and its nut.

clue.text: I go red all round, or a bit like another colour

indicators.note: all round means surrounding, so one piece wraps around the other

blocks.note: taken as written
to blush is to go red in the face

explanation.surface: Someone describes turning red all over, or perhaps a different shade.
explanation.walkthrough: The I sits inside BLUSH after its third letter, giving BLU-I-SH; the joke is that going red yields a shade of blue.
explanation.definitionFit: Bluish means somewhat blue, so slightly resembling a hue other than the red mentioned earlier.

clue.text: Barge is not so heavy

blocks.note: first meaning: a flat-bottomed boat for unloading ships
second meaning: of less weight

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a barge is a light vessel; in fact the noun is a separate meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun names a flat cargo boat used to ferry goods to and from ships, while the comparative adjective means weighing less.

clue.text: Spoiled, being wed, if one leaves

indicators.note: leaves means goes away, so that letter is removed from the word

blocks.note: someone wed is married
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A cynic remarks that marriage is ruined once a partner walks out.
explanation.definitionFit: Marred means damaged or impaired, so a thing spoiled has had its quality or appearance harmed.

clue.text: Force to join journalists’ team

blocks.note: the press is journalists collectively
a gang is a team of workers

explanation.surface: A newspaper's staff are being coerced into signing up.
explanation.definitionFit: Press gangs once seized men for naval service, so the verb means coerce someone into an activity against their will.

clue.text: Proposals advanced to hold dance

indicators.note: to hold means to contain, so the letters lie inside the neighbouring words

blocks.note: found across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Plans are put forward to stage a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: Salsa is a lively Latin American partner dance, also the name of its music.

clue.text: Possesses marijuana but not heroin

indicators.note: but not means without, so the named letter is taken away

blocks.note: hash is hashish, cannabis resin
H is slang for heroin

explanation.surface: A suspect is found holding cannabis but no harder drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: Has and possesses are synonymous verbs in the third person, both meaning owns or holds.

clue.text: In basement, vendor heard

indicators.note: heard means the word is identified by how it sounds when spoken

blocks.note: a vendor is a seller

explanation.surface: A trader is overheard downstairs.
explanation.definitionFit: A cellar is an underground room of a house, so a basement used for storage.

clue.text: Fall behind, walking route

blocks.note: first meaning: lag behind others
second meaning: a path for hikers

explanation.surface: A hiker drops back along the footpath.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means lag or straggle in a race, while as a noun it names a marked track through countryside.

clue.text: In the style of a West Coast city

blocks.note: taken as written
LA is Los Angeles, on the US West Coast

explanation.surface: Something is done after the manner of a Californian city.
explanation.definitionFit: The French borrowing 'à la' means after the manner of, as in à la mode or à la carte.

clue.text: Not so hairy a race? Nonsense

blocks.note: balder means having less hair
a dash is a short sprint

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a group of people is less hairy, and calls the idea rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'race' suggests an ethnic group, but it is a running contest.
explanation.definitionFit: Balderdash means senseless talk or writing, a synonym for rubbish or twaddle.
